status_note: Marker centres measured by registering the board photo to the printed artwork (scripts/register_print_artwork.py). Paper size from the print specification. Re-run perception.service --calibrate if markers were moved after the photo.
frame_note: UV frame = the UPRIGHT printed map as the team finalised it (landscape, map labels readable, river entering from the top): u to the right, v down, (0,0) at the paper's top-left corner, (1,1) at its bottom-right. NOTE FOR SHARED INTEGRATION: this print is landscape (height ~0.76 x width) while the scenario's board frame is a 420x420 square; the print-UV -> world board_uv/geo transform is owned by the shared lane and is NOT the identity.

board.dimensions_source: print specification 24 x 18 in; artwork aspect 0.7500

aruco.dictionary_note: Verified: all four printed markers decode in every 4X4 dictionary (50/100/250/1000 share these IDs). DICT_4X4_50 is used because it is the smallest family that contains them, which maximises decoding margin.
aruco.marker_size_note: Per-marker printed edges measured from the registered photo (mm). They differ, so registration uses the four measured centres (all four markers must be visible); the projector masks each marker by its own measured size.

photo_evidence.original: 5712x3213 phone photo supplied by the team on 2026-10-18 in the final landscape orientation (first supplied turned 90 deg)

12.note: its paper touches the image border; decodes via the padded retry

photo_evidence.derived: Layout TL=10, TR=11, BR=13, BL=12 (the legacy audit's assumed 12/13 order is swapped on the real board); all markers printed upright.

measured.notes: photo->artwork homography: 60 SIFT inliers, median 0.85 px
